name: headroom-project-conventions-v1
note: Original headroom tasks for the lesson-uplift A/B. Each task asks for a project-specific convention the base model CANNOT know unguided (an invented fact), so the off-arm fails and only an injected lesson supplies the answer — a clean headroom signal, unlike near-ceiling harness-enforced discipline. Tasks + lessons are authored for LocalBench; never copied from an external benchmark (clean-room). `lesson_ids` ties each task to the lesson(s) that supply its answer, for the injection assertion.

tasks.prompt: In the Larkspur service, what command applies pending database migrations?
In the Larkspur service, where are feature flags defined?
What prefix does the Larkspur release tooling require on a release tag?
What is the canonical command to run the Larkspur test suite?
What structured-logging field does Larkspur use to correlate requests?
Where does the Larkspur service read its API credentials from at runtime?

lessons.body: In the Larkspur service, apply pending database migrations with `lark db sync`. The older `lark migrate` command is deprecated and must not be used.
Larkspur feature flags are defined in `config/flags.toml`. Do not gate behaviour on environment variables; the flags file is the single source of truth.
Larkspur release tags must start with the `lk-` prefix (for example `lk-2026.06.1`). The release tooling rejects any tag without it.
Run the Larkspur test suite with `lark verify`. This wraps unit, integration, and contract tests; calling the underlying test framework directly skips the contract checks.
Larkspur correlates requests across services using the structured-logging field `trace_ref`. Always propagate `trace_ref`; never invent a new correlation field.
The Larkspur service reads API credentials at runtime from Vault under the path `/larkspur/runtime`. Credentials are never read from a `.env` file or baked into the image.
